observations: Photo shows a greasy, disassembled transmission/gearbox unit with attached wiring harness, sitting on bare ground outside a workshop.
A person in a branded t-shirt is working in the background; no clear shop signage or VIN/part tags visible.
No model plate, part number, or GMC logo is visible anywhere on the metal casing.
Unit appears heavily soiled and shows exposed connectors and hoses; some corrosion visible on metal surfaces.
Watermark 'GEARUP INT' overlays the image, seller/company branding not confirming the part's origin.

claims.claim: Direct America drive Gearbox for GMC Sierra V8 2008-2015
claims.evidence: No markings, tags, or VIN visible in photo 0 to confirm vehicle fitment or origin.
Seller's own title says 'Direct America' while the body text says 'direct from Belgium' — the two origin claims conflict within the same listing.
No video or audio of the unit running is provided; photo 0 only shows a static, disassembled part.
No odometer, service record, or seal/casing photo showing an unbroken factory seal.
No warranty document, receipt, or seller identity shown in photos.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition (gears, clutch packs, torque converter) could be worn or damaged despite claims of 'no knock'.
risks.proof: A video clip of the transmission running on a test stand or installed in a vehicle, showing smooth shifting and no noise.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needing rebuild

risks.risk: Origin mismatch (America vs Belgium) suggests possible misdescription or mixed-parts assembly, which can affect fitment and resale value.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any import/customs tag, shipping manifest, or VIN tag matching a GMC Sierra.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified origin, treated as generic used import

risks.risk: Completeness of the unit — missing solenoids, sensors, or torque converter could add hidden cost to make it usable.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all ports, connector plugs, and the torque converter bell housing from multiple angles.

risks.risk: Corrosion or water damage from storage outdoors could affect electronics and seals.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of internal casing, seals, and electrical connectors free of rust or water staining.
risks.if_unproven: priced as weather-exposed, higher refurbishment risk

proof_requests: Video of the gearbox running or shifting through gears on a test rig.
Clear photo of any VIN, part number, or manufacturer plate on the casing.
Photo or document showing import/customs origin (Belgium or America) to resolve the contradiction.
Close-up photos of the torque converter, solenoid pack, and all electrical connectors.
Photo showing the transmission installed or test-fitted in a GMC Sierra for fitment confirmation.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, but all seller claims about working condition, mileage, and origin are unverifiable from the single photo, and the origin claim is internally contradictory, so it must be priced at worst case pending proof.
